name: Yves Tumor
label: Warp
lede: Yves Tumor spent two and a half years on the road with Mykki Blanco, put out a record on Berlin's PAN, then signed to Warp and started getting compared to Prince.

eras.title: Knoxville, then Mykki's road
eras.text: Sean Lee Bowie grew up in Tennessee, left, and ended up in Los Angeles making post-chillwave as T.E.A.M.S. A two-and-a-half-year tour with Mykki Blanco then carried the project through Europe and Asia.

years.h: Sean Lee Bowie is born in Miami and raised in Knoxville
years.p: Tumor starts making music in his mid-teens, as a way out of what he calls dull, conservative surroundings.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has Bowie born in Miami on November 19, 1989, and raised in Knoxville, where he taught himself drums, bass, guitar and keyboards. It says he began making music at 16; a 2019 profile in Something Curated says 17.

He left Tennessee at 20, moving to San Diego and then Los Angeles after college. The name he records under, Yves Tumor, came later; before it, he worked as T.E.A.M.S.

years.h: Mykki Blanco puts him on the road for two and a half years
years.p: They meet in Los Angeles in 2012, and the collaboration turns into a tour of Europe and Asia.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and Something Curated both date the meeting to 2012, and both say the touring lasted about two and a half years. By then Bowie was still recording as T.E.A.M.S., which AllMusic described as post-chillwave.

Tumor appears on four tracks of Blanco's Mykki Blanco Presents C-ORE (2015): "Histrionic I," "Childish," "Histrionic II" and "Histrionic III / Skunk of the Earth."

years.h: T.E.A.M.S. gives way to Yves Tumor
years.p: Bowie shelves the post-chillwave name and starts over under the new one.

eras.title: Cassette first, Warp last
eras.text: A self-released cassette, a debut on Berlin's PAN, and a compilation that landed the same day Warp announced it had signed him.

years.h: When Man Fails You comes out on cassette first
years.p: His first release as Yves Tumor is self-released, and Apothecary Compositions reissues it on April 29, 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: Serpent Music · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Three years in, Serpent Music lands on PAN
years.p: Recorded across Miami, Leipzig, Los Angeles and Berlin. Pitchfork gave it 7.3 and Noisey ranked it No. 13 of 2016.
years.xp:
He had been calling the record "God Fearing" and kept it off Bandcamp so it wouldn't leak. After PAN founder Bill Kouligas praised the unfinished record, Tumor finished it for release. Wikipedia lists both September 22 and 23 for the date.

Metacritic scores it 77 from six reviews, and Pitchfork's Andy Beta compared the looped, field-recorded mood to James Ferraro and Dean Blunt.

years.big: "I never thought of it as soul music."
q: I never thought of it as soul music, but that's just what I was doing.
years.h: Soul, by accident
years.p: Tumor on Serpent Music, a record that grew out of the Motown and soul his father played in the house.
years.xp: Tumor told interviewers the record drew on personal relationships, spiritual themes and the music his father played when he was young. The finished album mixes soul, ambient, club, psychedelia and noise.

yt: Full set, Le Guess Who, Utrecht, November 2017
years.h: A compilation and a Warp deal arrive the same day
years.p: Experiencing the Deposit of Faith is self-released on September 13, 2017, the day Warp announces it has signed him.
years.xp: The compilation was self-released, so the Warp news and the record landed together. Two months later, on November 12, 2017, he played Le Guess Who in Utrecht, and a fan filmed the full set.

eras.title: The Warp debut
eras.text: The first Warp record turned up in September 2018 after three singles, and it made Tumor a name critics kept arguing over.

years.h: "Noid" comes with a video about police abuse
years.p: Warp's first Tumor single, directed by Andreas Brauning, follows him through downtown Los Angeles.
years.xp: The video follows Tumor through downtown Los Angeles and into police abuse. Rolling Stone called it a jarring examination of the police state.

years.src: Wikipedia: Safe in the Hands of Love · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Safe in the Hands of Love turns up on September 5
years.p: Three singles and a September 4 track from Warp came first. Pitchfork gave the album 9.1.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Paulie Sphere Sound in Mount Washington, Los Angeles, with Justin Raisen co-producing. The singles were "Noid" (July 24), "Licking an Orchid" with James K (August 29) and "Lifetime" (September 3).

Pitchfork's Jayson Greene wrote that it "dwarfs everything the artist has released by several orders of magnitude." Metacritic scores it 89; the CD and LP followed on October 12.

years.cap: Yves Tumor and band at a show, February 2019
years.h: A live band forms around Tumor
years.p: Yves Rothman (keys, musical director), Rhys Hastings (drums), Chris Greatti (lead guitar) and Gina Ramirez (bass) become the touring and recording group.

years.cap: Yves Tumor at All Points East, London, May 26, 2019
years.h: Tumor plays All Points East in London
years.p: Something Curated lists him at the festival on this date, in the wake of the Warp record.

years.h: Safe in the Hands of Love takes a Libera Award
years.p: At the 2019 Libera Awards it won Best Dance/Electronic Record, and was also nominated for Record of the Year and Best Outlier Record.

eras.title: Guitars arrive in lockdown
eras.text: Heaven to a Tortured Mind came out in the first month of lockdown and was written about as glam-rock and psychedelic soul. A shoegaze EP followed a year later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Heaven to a Tortured Mind · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Heaven to a Tortured Mind is out, with guitars and Pitchfork's No. 7
years.p: Justin Raisen and Mahssa Taghinia produce with Tumor. Metacritic scores it 88 from 18 reviews.
years.xp:
Singles were "Gospel for a New Century" (February 18), "Kerosene!" featuring Diana Gordon, and "Romanticist / Dream Palette" (March 19). The Guardian's Alexis Petridis made it Album of the Week, and Wikipedia notes comparisons to Prince and David Bowie.

Pitchfork's Kevin Lozano called it "a gratifying and intense record, one whose pleasures are viscerally immediate."

years.h: Locked down, he designs furniture and eyes welding
years.p: Tumor spends the pandemic on furniture, upholstery and architecture, and says he plans to move into welding construction.

years.h: Guest spots on Joji's "Reanimator" and a four-way jam
years.p: He features on "Reanimator" from Joji's Nectar, and on "Let All the Poisons That Lurk in the Mud Seep Out" with Kelsey Lu, Kelly Moran and Moses Boyd.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Asymptotical World · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: A year on, the Asymptotical World EP turns shoegaze
years.p: Tumor, Yves Rothman and new guitarist Chris Greatti share the instruments; Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and Loud and Quiet 9.
years.xp: The lead single "Jackie" came out June 15, 2021, and got compared to A.R. Kane and My Bloody Valentine. The video was nominated for a Video of the Year award in 2022. The EP wrote all tracks but "Tuck," which has lyrics co-written with Agnes Gryczkowska.

eras.title: Hot between worlds
eras.text: Tumor toured the world in 2022, sang on a Willow track, then released the album Pitchfork ranked No. 31 of 2023, with the live band behind it.

years.h: The 2022 world tour includes a Glastonbury set
years.p: Tumor tours internationally through 2022 with October and the Eyes, Timkoh and Doss, and sings on Willow's "Perfectly Not Close to Me" from Coping Mechanism.

years.cap: Yves Tumor at Positivus Festival, July 2022
years.h: "God Is a Circle" is the first sign of the next album
years.p: The first single from the coming Warp album, released with a dark video covered by NME.

yt: "Heaven Surrounds Us Like a Hood" official video
years.h: "Heaven Surrounds Us Like a Hood" gets a psychedelic video
years.p: The third single from the album, covered by The FADER and DIY.

years.src: Wikipedia: Praise a Lord · Wikipedia: Yves Tumor
years.h: Pitchfork scores Praise a Lord Who Chews... 8.4 and puts it at No. 31
years.p: Jayson Greene's review ranks the album No. 31 of 2023. Metacritic scores it 86 from 19 critics.
years.xp:
Produced by Tumor with Noah Goldstein, Simon Christensen, Elliott Kozel and Dylan Wiggins, the fifth album runs 37 minutes. The singles were "God Is a Circle," "Echolalia" (January 30), "Heaven Surrounds Us Like a Hood" and "Parody" (March 15).

Year-end lists put it No. 1 at Consequence, No. 4 at Vulture, No. 16 at The Guardian and No. 32 at Stereogum.
play: Praise a Lord Who Chews but Which Does Not Consume; (Or Simply, Hot Between Worlds)

years.h: Kanye West's Sunday Service choir sings on "Parody"
years.p: NPR notes that the Samples, the choir from West's Sunday Service, provide the vocals.

years.big: "It gives me life when something is made that no one saw happening."
q: It gives me life when something is made that no one saw happening.
years.h: NPR hears a private self set against a public one
years.p: The review reads Praise a Lord as private identity against public persona, in pop language from Motown to Prince.
years.xp: The NPR review says the record opens with a scream and ends on an invitation to lock eyes. It also notes Tumor told artist Kembra Pfahler: "I like to go on hikes and I like swimming."

years.cap: Yves Tumor live in New York, 2023
years.h: To Spite or Not to Spite starts in Indio and ends in Dublin
years.p: Dates run April 4 to November 27, 2023, with Pretty Sick, Frost Children, Izzy Spears, Evanora Unlimited and Nation opening.

eras.title: New guitarist, new collaborators, then allegations
eras.text: Maro Chon takes over lead guitar and Tumor posts a SoundCloud mixtape, then appears on records by Rosalía and Björk. In August 2026 the press reports allegations against him, which he denies.

years.h: Maro Chon replaces Chris Greatti on lead guitar
years.p: Wikipedia lists Greatti and Ramirez as 2019 to 2024 members and Chon as lead guitarist from 2024.

years.h: A SoundCloud mixtape, American Idol - The Greatest Notes Chapter 1
years.p: Released in 2024, off the Warp schedule.

years.h: Tumor and Björk both turn up on Rosalía's "Berghain"
years.p: The track is from Rosalía's Lux. Tumor also appears on a track with Nina called "We Don't Count."

years.h: Women accuse Tumor of assault; he calls it "100% untrue"
years.p: Stereogum and others report the allegations, including video from musician Angel Money. Tumor vowed legal action.
years.xp:
Stereogum reports an anonymous post on the Yves Tumor subreddit, Angel Money's video from a record-release party, and a statement from collaborator Kidä describing the experience in his touring band as "one of the most disrespectful professional experiences". The FADER and NME covered the accusations.

Tumor responded on Instagram, then in a follow-up called them "completely disgusting, salacious lies" from someone he barely knew. Stereogum's article mentions upcoming Bumbershoot dates but gives no cancellations or label response.
